title: Chemical equilibrium 2: shifts, Ks, Kv and industry - 123 school
heading: Chemical equilibrium 2: shifts, Ks, Kv and industry
intro: Choose the correct answer for each question. Use a calculator where needed.

questions.question: You add extra starting substance to an equilibrium. What happens?

answers.b: Q becomes greater than K and the equilibrium shifts to the right
answers.d: Q becomes smaller than K and the equilibrium shifts to the right

questions.question: You remove a reaction product from an equilibrium. What happens?

answers.c: the equilibrium shifts to the right
answers.d: the equilibrium shifts to the left

questions.question: What changes the value of K?

answers.a: the concentration of a starting substance

questions.question: You increase the pressure for N<sub>2</sub> (g) + 3 H<sub>2</sub> (g) ⇌ 2 NH<sub>3</sub> (g). What happens?

answers.b: the equilibrium shifts to the right
answers.d: the equilibrium shifts to the left

questions.question: For which equilibrium does an increase in pressure have no influence on the position?
You double the volume for 2 NO<sub>2</sub> (g) ⇌ N<sub>2</sub>O<sub>4</sub> (g). What happens?

answers.a: Q becomes greater than K and the equilibrium shifts to the left
answers.b: Q becomes smaller than K and the equilibrium shifts to the right

questions.question: You add a noble gas at constant volume to an equilibrium with gases. What happens?

answers.a: the equilibrium shifts to the left
answers.d: the equilibrium shifts to the right

questions.question: What does a catalyst do to an equilibrium?

answers.b: the equilibrium shifts to the right

questions.question: You increase the temperature of an equilibrium. Which way does it shift?

answers.b: towards the side with the most moles of gas

questions.question: For CaCO<sub>3</sub> (s) ⇌ CaO (s) + CO<sub>2</sub> (g) the reaction to the right is endothermic. You increase the temperature. What happens?

answers.b: K becomes greater and more CO<sub>2</sub> is formed
answers.c: K becomes smaller and more CO<sub>2</sub> is formed
answers.d: K becomes greater and less CO<sub>2</sub> is formed

questions.question: The formation of NH<sub>3</sub> is exothermic. You increase the temperature. What happens?

answers.a: K becomes smaller and the equilibrium shifts to the left
answers.b: K stays the same and the equilibrium shifts to the left
answers.c: K becomes greater and the equilibrium shifts to the right
answers.d: K becomes smaller and the equilibrium shifts to the right

questions.question: Why is about 450 °C used in ammonia production?

answers.a: NH<sub>3</sub> is liquid at that temperature
answers.b: the catalyst melts at that temperature
answers.c: a compromise between the position of the equilibrium and the reaction rate
answers.d: K is greatest at that temperature

questions.question: What is the catalyst in ammonia production?
Why is NH<sub>3</sub> continuously removed from the mixture in ammonia production?

answers.b: so the equilibrium keeps shifting to the right
answers.c: so the catalyst is not poisoned by the pressure

questions.question: What is the equilibrium condition for the solubility product of Ca(OH)<sub>2</sub>?
What is the equilibrium condition for the solubility product of Ca<sub>3</sub>(PO<sub>4</sub>)<sub>2</sub>?
For a salt MX (1 : 1), K<sub>s</sub> = 1.0·10<sup>–10</sup>. What is the solubility in pure water?
For a salt M(OH)<sub>2</sub>, K<sub>s</sub> = 4.0·10<sup>–6</sup>. What is the solubility in pure water?
When does a precipitate form when you mix two solutions?

answers.a: when Q is greater than K<sub>s</sub>
answers.b: when Q is smaller than K<sub>s</sub>

questions.question: In a solution [Ag<sup>+</sup>] = [Cl<sup>–</sup>] = 5.0·10<sup>–4</sup> mol/L. K<sub>s</sub> of AgCl is 1.8·10<sup>–10</sup>. What is Q and what happens?
Why does AgCl dissolve less well in NaCl solution than in water?

answers.a: K<sub>s</sub> becomes smaller due to NaCl
answers.c: extra Cl<sup>–</sup> shifts the equilibrium to the left

questions.question: K<sub>s</sub> of AgCl is 1.8·10<sup>–10</sup>. What is [Ag<sup>+</sup>] in a saturated solution with [Cl<sup>–</sup>] = 0.10 mol/L?
What does K<sub>v</sub> stand for?

answers.a: the formation equilibrium of a complex
answers.d: the distribution equilibrium of a substance over two immiscible liquids

questions.question: K<sub>v</sub> = [A] in hexane / [A] in water. At equilibrium [A] in water is 0.020 mol/L and in hexane 1.0 mol/L. What is K<sub>v</sub>?
K<sub>v</sub> = [A] in hexane / [A] in water = 40. In water [A] = 0.010 mol/L. What is [A] in hexane?
What is favourable when extracting a substance from water with an extraction agent?

answers.a: an extraction agent that mixes with water

questions.question: You want to extract as much substance as possible from water with a total of 100 mL of extraction agent. What is the smartest?

answers.d: first heat the extraction agent until boiling
